prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (RDC, alias/call sign Juniper) continuously intakes emergency medical requests via controlled intake creating incident records, provides triage support, dispatch, regional coordination/shared operational picture; translates reports into prioritized incidents under approved clinical/jurisdictional protocols. Jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy. Area divided into response zones; boundaries maintained/reviewed after road, population, agreement changes. Dispatch decisions shall reflect distance, access, travel time, restrictions, weather, closures, ambulance capacity. Zone routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center follow clinical direction/current access; crews verify constrained routes.

Actors/elements: Call Taker Mara (radio alias Larkspur) uses Computer Aided Dispatch Console (CAD) to enter assessment requests/incident data, establishes location before medical details: address, municipality, building/floor/entrance, repeats/checks landmarks, asks callback, patient age/consciousness/breathing/main complaint, distinguishes observed vs reported symptoms, records symptom onset if reliable, notes access barriers, remains engaged if info could change priority/access plan, produces Caller Location Correction Slip when address needs documented clarification. CAD supports dispatch, checks location against address/map data; staff remain responsible for currency; unresolved locations require focused follow-up and incident update.

Triage Supervisor assigns/confirms priority, requests clinical review, coordinates prioritization with operations when demand/access changes. Regional Medical Director sets clinical triage policy/limits; seek guidance beyond delegated authority. Shift Commander (Sundial) on-duty operational authority for continuity, surge priorities, conflicts, escalation; reviews readiness concerns for repositioning/coverage plan changes; not RMD/crew authority. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) manages Regional Radio Network, channels/backup/radio checks. Paramedic Crew assesses/cares, reports access barriers and vehicle readiness concerns.

Ambulance Coordination Platform provides shared view of incidents, assignments, zone coverage, unit availability/resources. Hospital Liaison Desk (coordination alias Kestrel) coordinates receiving capacity/destination constraints; Emergency Department/Riverside Trauma Center receive considerations. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay) monitors vehicle availability/servicing/defects/constraints, produces Battery Swap Voucher. Gate boards produce/access North Approach Queue Snapshot/status.

Readiness checks cover staffing, comms, supplies, fuel, vehicle condition, maintenance restrictions; reassess after significant incidents, interruptions, route/access changes. RDC compares reported conditions with coverage and escalates unresolved readiness gaps to operational lead.

New part:
S066: The Hospital Liaison Desk supports intake coordination by confirming facility capabilities and clarifying hospital contact pathways.
S067: The Hospital Liaison Desk checks whether a reported destination preference is compatible with current facility capabilities.
S068: When a facility constraint affects coordination, the Hospital Liaison Desk records the constraint in the incident notes.
S069: The Hospital Liaison Desk produces the Bedside Arrival Receipt when an ambulance arrival has been confirmed.
S070: The Hospital Liaison Desk provides current facility information through established coordination channels without delaying emergency call intake.
S071: The Triage Supervisor reviews incidents when the reported symptoms or uncertainty warrant clinical escalation.
S072: The Data Quality Officer monitors intake records for recurring gaps in location or medical detail.
S073: Call Taker Mara updates the incident record when a caller provides new information before dispatch decisions are finalized.
S074: The Regional Dispatch Center preserves the original caller report alongside subsequent clarifications so responders can distinguish confirmed details from estimates.
S075: Clinical triage begins after Call Taker Mara has captured the caller's reported symptoms, location, and immediate hazards.
S076: The recorded information provides an initial basis for assigning urgency and does not replace clinical reassessment as new information arrives.
S077: Triage Supervisor reviews incidents with uncertain severity, conflicting reports, or signs of rapid deterioration.
S078: Priority is based on the immediacy of threat to life, the likely time sensitivity of care, and the risk of deterioration while awaiting response.
S079: Incidents indicating an immediate threat receive the highest available response priority and prompt dispatch action.
S080: Incidents without an immediate threat are prioritized according to the expected harm from delay and the patient's reported condition.
S081: When essential information is missing, Triage Supervisor directs focused clarification while ensuring that information gathering does not delay an urgent response.
S082: Triage Supervisor escalates clinically ambiguous or unusually severe cases to Regional Medical Director for guidance when time permits.
S083: Regional Medical Director provides clinical policy guidance and does not replace the operational authority responsible for dispatch decisions.
S084: Triage Supervisor sends the Pediatric Acuity Note.
S085: Triage Supervisor is known operationally as Copperfield.
S086: Data Quality Officer is known operationally as Pebble.
S087: Data Quality Officer monitors incident records for missing, inconsistent, or duplicated information that could impair triage or dispatch.
S088: Data Quality Officer sends the Duplicate Incident Audit Memo.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
